<thought>Based on the molecular formula C5H11O3Br and the saturated nature (DBE = 0), a plausible way to split the molecule is into an ethyl‑bromide fragment and a glycerol fragment. These two fragments together contain the required atoms and can be joined by forming a C–C bond, losing two hydrogens in the process, which matches the observed hydrogen count. Therefore the fragments are represented by the SMILES strings “CCBr” (ethyl bromide) and “C(CO)CO” (glycerol).</thought>
<final_answer>['CCBr', 'C(CO)CO']</final_answer>
